title: 'They are now athletes' - how do referees get ready for a season?
description: Pre-season camps in Spain and full-time training throughout the season - the rigorous regimes top-flight officials undergo to keep up with the pace of play in the Premier League
fullText:
Referees know every decision will be scrutinised.

Fans, pundits and players will pore over their calls, creating never-ending debates.

Many of the Professional Referee Group, the top officials in the country, have met in Loughborough this week.

They meet every few weeks to work and train together, with the officials spread across the country.

Lunch is a choice of chicken, teriyaki beef or tofu with vegetables and salad, with protein bars and rice cakes alongside the fruit, granola and Greek yogurts.

It is a reminder of the environment. Since becoming professional in 2001 top flight officials have had to adapt.

"I never thought referees did as much as what we do now," says Sam Allison, who played for Chippenham Town and Frome Town during his playing career, which started at Swindon.

"We are training full-time, sometimes two, three sessions a day, making sure that we are ready on a Saturday afternoon.

"Some of it (not understanding referees' workload) is probably ignorance, lack of awareness, lack of communication being disseminated to people out there.

"I think of my ignorance of just thinking referees just turned up, refereed the game and then went home.

"We have all the preparation, all the training, all the sacrifices, all the commitment, all the desire, all the support networks, people investing in you to make sure that you are ready in the best position to deliver a game."

Allison, a former firefighter, is the fourth official for Manchester City's trip to Crystal Palace on Friday while colleague Sam Barrott has been given Saturday's early match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest.

Barrott took charge of Arsenal's Community Shield win over Manchester City this month and was in the Faroe Islands on 20 August to referee Ki Klaksvik's 0-0 draw with Riga in the Europa Conference League.

Different teams and different tactics means a different approach to each game, with officials prepping with Pro Ref's analysis team who provide key information to understand the way a team is going to play, to support the flow of the game.

It comes after a summer of work to ensure the officials can match - and better - the demands of the Premier League.

"At the moment we've got five substitutions and we see all the time fresh legs for teams can change the momentum in a game," said Barrott.

"If three new attacking players are on that are all very pacey after 70 minutes you know they're going to change the way they play, they're going to try and push.

"That normally means an increase in output for us and when that happens, there's not a point in us where we go, we can't handle this'.

"We've been trying to push the demands of where we are, everybody's trying to get better. Football has the 1% gains, every game or every training session we're very similar in the mindset, we want to be better."

Francis Bunce has been with Pro Ref - rebranded from the Professional Game Match Officials Limited - for 10 years and is now the physical performance manager.

He was with the group in Spain last month for their pre-season training camp, putting them through what is viewed as the infamous Maximal Aerobic Speed (MAS) test - an all out six-minute run.

"When you look at refereeing in the Premier League and Championship people very rarely talk about their physical qualities or physical capabilities," he tells BBC Sport.

"They've all done so well to keep developing and they look like athletes on the pitch - they are athletes.

"We're in a very different space with match officials, they are naturally some years older than the players and you can't get away from that because having a 21-year-old referee would be very difficult in the Premier League with everything you need to learn and experience.

"They should be definitely considered as athletes and if you then compare them to Joe Public who might want to shout some views from the sidelines, they wouldn't be able to keep up for a minute with what some of our guys can do."

With officials training remotely for part of the week, they need to be monitored with heart rate and GPS technology.

All the officials are on tailored plans and work in a group of around five once or twice a week at local hubs where strength and conditioning sessions are delivered.

Those at the World Cup - referees Michael Oliver and Anthony Taylor, along with assistants Gary Beswick, Adam Nunn, Stuart Burt and James Mainwaring - also had special training this summer, running and cycling in chambers of around 40 degrees to prepare them for the intense heat at the tournament.

Last season referees ran a total of 3.6m metres, with their overall sprint distance 12,136m.

At the weekend, Stuart Attwell covered the fourth highest distance of anyone on the pitch while taking charge of Newcastle's 2-2 draw with Liverpool, awarding the Reds a stoppage time penalty.

He was also fifth for highest high-speed running, therefore beating all but four players.

"A lot of people could go and run around the pitch but they wouldn't be able to pick up those key positions to make those defining decisions," says Bunce.

"That's something that's really important we build into our training, in terms of how we improve speed, how we improve being able to physically exert that kind of acceleration or high-speed running into a game.

"Then make a decision and to do it in a cool, calm manner and potentially have to make a VAR announcement and sound completely like they haven't been running around for 90 minutes."

The work pays off with Barrott recalling an incident in a match between Brighton and Fulham which underlined why it is worth it.

It came in March 2025 when he awarded a late penalty after Harrison Reed fouled Joao Pedro and the striker scored the injury-time penalty to earn the Seagulls a 2-1 win.

"I'm stood at the edge of the box, everyone turns and you're pointing at the penalty spot. There wasn't anything in me that thought 'you've got that wrong'," says Barrott.

"It was complete confidence, all because I'm stood in the right spot and to do that. It involves a little bit of football knowledge, anticipating what could happen and what we would call a danger area.

"But then also knowing what you've done for weeks and weeks - and potentially years and years - has allowed you to move into that position without having to think.

"It's just subconscious, it just happens and you're not stood there thinking: 'I'm tired, do I need to make that run?'

"That never comes into the thought process anymore, and the fatigue aspect of it never crosses your mind because we are where we need to be."

title: Departing Watkins apologised for refusing to play - Emery
description: Ollie Watkins is leaving Aston Villa as their record Premier League goalscorer.
fullText:
Manager Unai Emery said Ollie Watkins apologised for refusing to play for Aston Villa on Sunday as he paid an emotional tribute to the departing striker.

The 30-year-old is expected in Saudi Arabia on Friday to complete a £51m move to Al-Hilal, with Villa poised to finalise the signing of Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson for £65m as his replacement.

Emery praised the England forward's behaviour during his Villa career and said he and the squad had accepted Watkins' apology for making himself unavailable against Brighton.

Watkins is Villa's record Premier League scorer with 91 goals, part an overall tally of 108 in all competitions since signing from Brentford for £28m in 2020.

"He told us after the Brighton match he was sorry and that he had made a mistake. He was wrong, but we accepted it. The players as well," said Emery.

"His commitment and his behaviour was fantastic. He's a fantastic guy - a fantastic guy even more than a player. I told him 'bye' with a huge hug and with small tears.

"But now it's a new chapter here with Nicolas Jackson."

Villa have agreed a deal for Jackson and are trying to ensure the Senegal striker is registered for Monday's visit of Arsenal.

Watkins is the latest experienced player to leave Villa this summer and Emery urged supporters to back the club's strategy despite the loss of several key figures in their successful 2025-26 season.

"We took decisions because it's good for the club," Emery said.

"Of course, we don't want to be a club that sells players, but the responsibility is there. It's crazy [money for someone] 30 years old and £50m for Ezri Konsa [who is 28].

"How we developed in the last year with some players and how we can sell some players now is completely the right decision.

"We have to rebuild the team as fast as possible. [Fans] have to accept our way and why we are taking some decisions."

As part of the rebuild, Leon Goretzka completed his move on a free transfer to Villa on Thursday after leaving Bayern Munich at the end of last season.

The midfielder won seven Bundesliga titles and the Champions League with Bayern.

"He is a winner. He is a very competitive player - a good player to add into our squad," said Emery.

"He is versatile and arrives fit and training well. Hopefully on Monday he can be on the field."

title: Sutton's predictions v Royal Blood drummer Ben Thatcher
description: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on Royal Blood drummer Ben Thatcher, plus the BBC readers and AI with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.
fullText:
Defending champions Arsenal made an impressive start to the season against newly promoted Coventry but face a tougher test against Aston Villa on Monday.

But with the number of outgoings at Villa Park, will it be another eye-opener for Unai Emery's men after last week's heavy defeat by Brighton?

"Aston Villa had a slow start last season, they have lost big players and I just think Arsenal are going to run all over teams this season.

"I think they are going to get better and better which is ominous for everybody else."

"We loved Danny, because he really fitted into our style of play and he had such a great season last year," Ben told BBC Sport.

"We will miss Van Hecke at the back too, but the thing with Brighton is that we always bounce back. We always come through with the players we bring in that I've never heard of, but they get given this chance.

"I just trust in [Brighton owner] Tony Bloom. He knows better than anyone about these things, because he has done it so many times before.

"He has sold so many world-class players to other clubs and we have nurtured so many great players to replace them.

"So, I don't feel there is any need to worry right now. Just put the trust in the club and see how we get on.

"It's great to be back in Europe [in the Europa Conference League] but with us potentially playing so many more games, I don't expect us to get there again through our league position this time.

"But my hope is that we won't drop into the bottom half of the table. My thinking is that, as long as we finish in the top 10 again and have a good go at Europe, then that's a great season."

I still think they're good enough to stay up - they've got Granit Xhaka and some other good players. I like that they are physical and aggressive.

With respect, it was an open goal start for the season for them, with Hull then Ipswich - two promoted sides - and it would be bordering on catastrophic for Michael Carrick if they lose again.

title: Man City and Aston Villa to face holders PSG in Champions League
description: European champions Paris St-Germain will face Premier League duo Manchester City and Aston Villa in the league phase of this season's Champions League.
fullText:
European champions Paris St-Germain will face Premier League duo Manchester City and Aston Villa as well as five-time winners Barcelona in the league phase of this season's Champions League.

The back-to-back Champions League winners will welcome Barca to Parc des Princes, while they were also handed trips to Villa Park and Manchester in the draw for the league phase.

Premier League champions Arsenal, meanwhile, will host 15-time winners Real Madrid at Emirates Stadium, and have also been handed a trip to Bayern Munich.

Mikel Arteta's men, who were beaten by PSG on penalties in the final last season, will face Borussia Dortmund, Real Betis, Lille, Napoli, Azerbaijan champions Sabah and Slavia Prague as well.

Enzo Maresca's City will welcome PSG to Etihad Stadium and travel to Barcelona, where they will have a reunion with Spanish World Cup-winner Rodri, who moved to the Nou Camp in a £65m deal this summer.

City will also be up against another of their former midfielders in Kevin de Bruyne when Napoli visit Manchester, with Sporting, Porto, RB Leipzig, AEK Athens and Lens their other opponents.

Europa League winners Villa, returning to the competition after a season away, will host PSG and Dortmund and travel to Barcelona and Galatasaray.

Unai Emery's side also face Club Brugge, Fenerbahce, Viking and Slavia Prague.

Manchester United, returning after a two-year hiatus, will meet Bayern, Atletico Madrid, Roma, Sporting, Leipzig, Villarreal, Sabah and Como.

Liverpool, meanwhile, host Atletico, Porto, Villarreal and Lens while visiting Inter Milan, Brugge, Fenerbahce and LASK.

The first league-phase matches will be played on Tuesday, 8 September and the last round of games will take place on 27 January 2027, with the exact schedule to be released on Saturday.

This season's final will be held in Madrid on 5 June.

Arsenal: Real Madrid (home), Bayern Munich (away), Borussia Dortmund (home), Real Betis (away), Lille (home), Napoli (away), Sabah (home), Slavia Prague (away)

Aston Villa: PSG (home), Barcelona (away), Borussia Dortmund (home), Club Brugge (away), Fenerbahce (home), Galatasaray (away), Viking (home), Slavia Prague (away)

Liverpool: Atletico Madrid (home), Inter Milan (away), Porto (home), Club Brugge (away), Villarreal (home), Fenerbahce (away), Lens (home), LASK (away)

Manchester City: PSG (home), Barcelona (away), Sporting Club (home), Porto (away), Napoli (home), Leipzig (away), AEK Athens (home), Lens (away)

Manchester United: Bayern Munich (home), Atletico Madrid (away), Roma (home), Sporting Club (away), Leipzig (home), Villarreal (away), Sabah (home), Como (away)

Each of the 36 teams plays eight different teams - four at home and four away - in the league phase.

Teams who finish in the top eight automatically qualify for the last 16, while those placing ninth to 24th will compete in a two-legged knockout play-off for the chance to join them.

Sides who finish 25th or lower will be eliminated, and will not drop into the Europa League.

Last season, eventual runners-up Arsenal topped the league phase standings with 24 points after eight wins from as many matches.

Liverpool were third - behind second-placed Bayern Munich - with 18 points while Tottenham finished one point behind in fourth.

Chelsea and Manchester City also qualified directly for the last 16 after finishing sixth and eighth respectively while Newcastle finished 12th.

Chelsea, Manchester City, Newcastle and Spurs were knocked out in the last 16 last season while Liverpool were beaten in the quarter-finals by PSG, who also edged Arsenal in the final for their second consecutive title.

title: Fan backlash as gay World Cup star joins Saudi club
description: Spain forward Esther Gonzalez attracts backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.
fullText:
Spain forward Esther Gonzalez has attracted backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.

The 33-year-old agreed a mutual contract termination with National Women's Soccer League champions Gotham FC in July to temporarily step away from the sport to "attend to personal matters in Spain", according to the club's statement.

Gonzalez, whose contract was due to expire in 2027, said on Instagram the decision was "due to strictly personal reasons", adding New York-based Gotham will "always hold a special place in my heart".

However, on Sunday, Al Qadsiah announced the signing of the 2023 World Cup winner, sparking criticism from both Gotham fans over the nature of her departure, and from within the LGBTQ+ community.

Same-sex relationships and sexual activity are illegal in Saudi Arabia.

Fans on social media questioned her motivations and expressed concerns for her safety while Gotham supporters voiced their disappointment over the messaging around her exit and the club missing out on a transfer fee.

According to Spanish outlet El Mundo,, external Gonzalez has deleted all photos of herself with her wife and their first child, born in January, from her social media accounts since signing for Al Qadsiah.

Gonzalez is not the first footballer to encounter negative reactions for moving to Saudi Arabia, with England midfielder Jordan Henderson attracting criticism following his transfer to Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq in 2023.

The move was described as a "slap in the face" by openly gay footballer Jake Daniels, who had received a message of support from Henderson when he came out.

The former Liverpool captain, who had previously shown his support for the LGBTQ+ community by wearing rainbow laces, a One Love armband, and writing messages of solidarity in a matchday programme, left Al-Ettifaq after six months.

Gonzalez won two NWSL titles, an NWSL Challenge Cup, and the Concacaf W Champions Cup in three seasons after moving to the United States from Real Madrid.

Al Qadsiah finished fourth in the Saudi Women's Premier League in 2025-26.

title: Will a Premier League club break record for transfer sales in one window?
description: Aston Villa, Manchester City and Newcastle are closing in on Monaco's record for transfer income generated in a single window.
fullText:
Premier League clubs are usually associated with spending heavily in the transfer market, but this summer several have been making as much noise through their sales.

Aston Villa, Manchester City and Newcastle United have already moved into the all-time top six for transfer income generated in a single window, with Monaco's 360m euros haul from 2018-19 now within reach.

Monaco's record was built around several major departures, most notably Kylian Mbappe's 180m euros move to Paris St-Germain, while Thomas Lemar joined Atletico Madrid for 72m euros and Fabinho moved to Liverpool for 45m euros.

On 26 August, according to Transfermarkt, which lists transfer fees in euros, Villa have brought in 293.1m euros (£251m) from departures this summer, City 278.6m euros and Newcastle 275.5m euros.

Only Monaco, Chelsea's 321m euros in 2025-26 and Atletico Madrid's 314m euros in 2019-20 currently sit above them.

And with several days of the window still remaining, the record could yet fall.

Villa are currently closest to Monaco with Morgan Rogers' £117m (138m euros) move to Chelsea accounting for a significant chunk of their total. Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne were also among those to leave.

Their summer trading has also left them with the strongest positive transfer balance in the Premier League.

Villa have spent 160.5m euros, which leaves them 132.6m euros in profit on transfer dealings. That activity comes against a backdrop of financial pressure.

In June, Villa were fined 22.5m euros by Uefa for a significant breach of its squad-cost rule for 2025, with 15m euros of that amount suspended on the condition that the club continued to reduce its squad-cost ratio during 2026.

The impact of losing several senior players was evident on the opening weekend, when Unai Emery's side suffered a 4-0 defeat by Brighton.

Speaking afterwards, Gary Neville said Villa looked as though they had had their "heart ripped out", pointing to the experience lost through the departures of Rogers, Tielemans and Konsa.

Villa could yet move even closer to the record.

Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal have made several attempts to sign Ollie Watkins, with Villa reportedly rejecting an offer worth around 52m euros. Emery has already acknowledged that the England striker could leave, although the two clubs remain apart on valuation.

Manchester City's position has shifted following Wednesday's signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi. They have generated 278.5m euros from sales so far, with the departures of players including Savio, Tijjani Reijnders, Rodri, James Trafford, Manuel Akanji and Nathan Ake.

Bouaddi's arrival takes City's spending to 273.7m euros, leaving them with a positive transfer balance of 4.8m euros.

Further departures could quickly change the picture again. Tottenham have agreed a loan deal to sign Omar Marmoush, with an obligation to make the move permanent for £60m (58m euros) next summer. That fee would therefore count towards City's 2027-28 transfer income rather than this season's figures.

Nico Gonzalez is also expected to leave, while Jack Grealish could yet be another departure before the deadline. Grealish spent last season on loan at Everton, who remain interested, although the winger has viewed Enzo Maresca replacing Pep Guardiola as manager as a fresh start at City. His contract runs until June 2027.

A permanent sale of Gonzalez, and possibly Grealish, could still significantly increase City's 2026-27 income.

Their ability to sell at such a level is particularly significant given the scale of their midfield rebuild. City have already signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for 135m euros. They also remain interested in Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

Newcastle have reached 275.5m euros in sales with the bulk of that coming from three major departures.

Sandro Tonali joined Tottenham for 108m euros, Bruno Guimaraes moved to Arsenal for 87.5m euros and Anthony Gordon signed for Barcelona for 80m euros.

Together, those deals have transformed Newcastle's summer balance sheet.

They have spent 197m euros, which leaves them 78.5m euros in profit.

Only Villa and Nottingham Forest currently have a larger positive transfer balance among Premier League clubs.

The volume of sales across the division is reflected in the wider transfer balances.

Six Premier League clubs currently have a positive balance, according to Transfermarkt:

At the other end of the scale, Chelsea have the largest negative balance at 242.3m euros after spending 407.95m euros and receiving 165.65m euros.

Tottenham are next at 189.15m euros in the red, followed by Arsenal at 180.95m euros with several days until the transfer window closes on 1 September.

Brighton's sales figures illustrate a different approach.

Over the past five seasons, Brighton have spent 665.4m euros on players and received 715.4m euros in transfer fees, leaving them with a positive transfer balance of about 50m euros.

According to Transfermarkt, they are the only current Premier League club to have made a cumulative transfer profit across that five-season period. Aston Villa are the next closest to break-even, with an overall balance of -10.02m euros.

That underlines how consistently Brighton have combined significant player sales with reinvestment, rather than relying on one unusually profitable window.

title: When is the EFL Cup third-round draw?
description: Nine Premier League clubs taking part in European football join the 23 first-round winners from across the English Football League.  Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Sunderland, Brighton and Crystal Palace will enter the competition at this stage, as the top eight Premier League clubs from the 2025-26 season plus Crystal Palace as Conference League winners.
fullText:
The third-round draw for the 2026-27 Carabao Cup will take place on Wednesday, 26 August following the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nine Premier League clubs taking part in European football join the 23 first-round winners from across the English Football League.

Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Sunderland, Brighton and Crystal Palace will enter the competition at this stage, as the top eight Premier League clubs from the 2025-26 season plus Crystal Palace as Conference League winners.

It will be broadcast live on Sky Sports following the conclusion of the third round tie between Preston North End and Everton, kicking off at 20:00 BST.

Unlike the opening two rounds of the competition, the third round draw is not regionalised.

However, before the match at Deepdale there will be a pre-draw determining which of the Champions League and Europa League clubs will play at home or away in round three.

In order to avoid potential scheduling issues, the eight Champions League and Europa League clubs cannot be drawn against each other in round three.

When the draw takes place, the first eight fixtures decided are the ones involving clubs in the Champions League and Europa League. The remainder of the draw will be an open draw as usual.

Due to clashes with opening weeks of the Champions League and Europa League seasons, the third round will be played across two different weeks. They are the weeks commencing Monday, 7 and Monday, 14 September, 2026.

title: Manchester United preparing €30 million offer for Barcelona defender
description: Manchester United could make a late move for Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde, with a new report from El Larguero claiming that the Premier League club is preparing a potential €30 million offer b...
fullText:
Manchester United could make a late move for Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde, with a new report from El Larguero claiming that the Premier League club is preparing a potential €30 million offer before the transfer window closes.

The future of the 22-year-old left-back has attracted growing attention in recent weeks, particularly amid reports of a change in his relationship with Barcelona manager Hansi Flick.

While there has been no suggestion that Flick has directly told Balde to leave, the German has indeed urged the defender to raise his level and improve his focus during what could be an important season for his development.

That situation has opened the door to speculation over a possible transfer, although Balde himself is not understood to be actively seeking an exit from Barcelona.

According to El Larguero, an intermediary with international contacts has indicated that Manchester United are considering a €30 million proposal for Balde.

The potential bid is being prepared for the closing stages of the transfer window.

Manchester United are preparing an offer for Alejandro Balde. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images)

Barcelona, for their part, would be willing to study an offer in the region of €30-35 million, provided Balde is also open to the move.

That leaves room for negotiations should a formal proposal arrive from Old Trafford.

The key factor, though, could ultimately be the player's own decision.

Despite recent uncertainty surrounding his role, Balde remains determined to fight for his place at Barcelona.

The Spanish international believes he can still convince Flick and is not willing to leave the club simply because his position in the squad has become less secure.

At 22, Balde still has plenty of time on his side and the potential to regain the confidence of his manager.

Balde is not pushing to leave Barcelona. (Photo by Judit Cartiel/Getty Images)

He appears to see the current situation as a challenge rather than a reason to seek a new destination immediately.

In fact, reports suggest he would only consider leaving Barcelona if a genuinely attractive opportunity emerged. As things stand, he is not actively pushing for a transfer.

Barcelona are also believed to be relatively well prepared for a possible departure.

The club has enough options to cover the left-back position, including Joao Cancelo and Gerard Martin, so they would not necessarily be left short if Balde were to move on.

Still, his exit is far from a certainty. Barcelona may be prepared to consider the right financial proposal, but the player's desire to remain and prove himself under Flick remains a major part of the equation.

title: Bruno Fernandes and Khadija Shaw win PFA Player of the Year awards
description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year as Manchester City's Khadija Shaw won the women's award for the second time. Playmaker Fernandes broke the all-time record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.
fullText:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year as Manchester City's Khadija Shaw won the women's award for the second time.

Playmaker Fernandes broke the all-time record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcome a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick and earn a Champions League return.

Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals.

He said: "It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it's probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment."

The Portugal international is the Red Devils' first winner since Wayne Rooney took home the trophy in 2009-10 and adds to his Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year award from May.

Manchester City sharpshooter Shaw, who was also recognized by the FWA, scooped the PFA Women's Player of the Year award for the second time.

The 29-year-old claimed the trophy in 2023-24 and won it again having scored 21 goals on the way to a third straight Golden Boot and her maiden Women's Super League title.

Arsenal's Olivia Smith picked up the women's PFA Young Player of the Year title for the second campaign running, having won the 2025 crown for her exploits at Liverpool and continued her form in the capital.

Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly was named men's PFA Young Player of the Year following an outstanding campaign that ended with the versatile talent helping England to win World Cup bronze.

The 21-year-old was part of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year along with City team-mates Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo.

O'Reilly said: "I had a great season. I'm very proud of the season I had. I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I'm over the moon how it turned out."

Champions Arsenal had five representatives in David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice, with Player of the Year Fernandes of United and Brentford's Igor Thiago completing the team.

The PFA WSL Team of the Year featured three players from triumphant City, with Shaw joined by team-mates Kerstin Casparij and Yui Hasegawa.

Mariona Caldentey, last year's PFA Women's Player of the Year, was joined in the XI by fellow Arsenal players Emily Fox and Alessia Russo.

Tottenham defender Toko Koga and Manchester United's Jess Park were also included in a team, as were the Chelsea trio of Hannah Hampton, Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James.

Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney received the PFA merit awards in recognition of their contribution to football.

Dalglish enjoyed a success-laden career as player with Celtic and Liverpool, and is Scotland's most capped player having represented his country on 102 occasions.

The 75-year-old, who confirmed in June he was undergoing treatment for cancer, went on to enjoy a successful managerial career, leading Liverpool to three league titles before masterminding Blackburn's Premier League triumph.

Carney played 144 times for England, including being part of the Lionesses squad which finished third at the 2015 World Cup.

Having come through the ranks at Birmingham, Carney won the quadruple with Arsenal in 2007 as well as a league and FA Cup double with Chelsea in 2018.

title: How did all nine new managers fare in Premier League openers?
description: Who impressed and who has work to do? BBC Sport chief football writer Phil McNulty looks at how the nine new managerial appointments fared on the opening week of the Premier League season.
fullText:
Premier League history was made before a ball was even kicked this season as a record nine clubs started the season with new managers.

The post-Pep Guardiola era has begun at Manchester City under Enzo Maresca, while Andoni Iraola got his first taste of action as Liverpool manager after succeeding sacked Arne Slot. Xabi Alonso is the latest with his foot in the revolving door of managers at Chelsea.

So how did the new faces fare after an eventful first weekend of the new campaign?

The German successor to Iraola came within six minutes of starting his Premier League career with a statement win at Manchester City, only to concede two late goals to suffer a heartbreaking loss.

He will be frustrated at the manner of City's goals, with Marc Guehi unmarked at a corner for the equaliser then a slow reaction for Josko Gvardiol's stoppage time winner, but Rose was also shown in those first 84 minutes that he has plenty of materials to work with in a Cherries side that finished sixth last season.

Rose will have seen enough to deliver early signs of encouragement amid the disappointment of such a painful late loss.

Not a bad start to take the lead after 31 seconds and a satisfactory start to Alonso's reign, but there was obvious good and obvious bad in what he watched at Craven Cottage.

The attacking triumvirate of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and newcomer Morgan Rogers hit the ground running, all scoring and combining to devastating effect.

Equally devastating to Chelsea's Premier League chances and the Alonso revival could be the failure to find a better goalkeeper than the unreliable Robert Sanchez, who was at fault for both Fulham goals.

Alonso must find an answer quickly otherwise what Palmer, Joao Pedro and Rogers give with one hand Sanchez could take away with both hands.

Tactically Alonso used a back three with Reece James operating in midfield but also dropping back into defence.

Disappointing start for the highly-regarded Sage, who did such an outstanding job at Lens, with defeat at Everton but he also knows the outcome could have been a much more satisfactory one.

Palace's second half display will have disappointed him, but they had chances in the opening period to set up their first win at Everton since 2014. They hit the woodwork twice, while Jean-Phillipe Mateta was wasteful. Sage and his team paid a heavy price.

Sage's unhappy opening weekend will not have been helped by a contract row surrounding striker Mateta that puts his future in question, while he will want more numbers and quality to add to his squad.

Next up Manchester City at Selhurst Park, where Sage will sample the superb night game atmosphere as he searches for his first league win. No easy task.

Tough opener and conceding within the first minute did not help Arbeloa's cause as he builds after taking over from Marco Silva.

It is already clear he needs to make sure Fulham can find some goals, although he will be delighted young debutant Gonzalo Garcia got off the mark. It was more of a struggle for another new arrival from Real Madrid, Cesar Palacios.

The jewel in Arbeloa's crown will be 19-year-old Josh King, who he described as "unbelievable". It is already clear the youngster will bear a heavy weight of responsibility under Fulham's new management.

Ipswich Town have backed Kieran McKenna's successor with big money in the transfer market, £150m on a dozen signings, and Gary O'Neil was rewarded with a vital victory against Sunderland.

O'Neil may just be the beneficiary from lessons learned during Ipswich's last spell in the Premier League, when they took 11 games to get a win and went down with a whimper with just 22 points.

He will have been delighted with the impact of Julio Enciso, who he worked with at Strasbourg, and his early partnership with Brazilian striker Emersonn, the pair combining superbly for the latter's opening goal.

Plenty still to work on but O'Neil looked in the mood to enjoy his cup of tea and bar of chocolate while watching Match Of The Day on Saturday night.

Iraola was spared the ignominy of defeat in his first Premier League game since succeeding Arne Slot by Dominik Szoboszlai's 99th minute penalty – but this was a sobering fact-finding mission for the new man in charge at Anfield.

He did not seem unduly concerned, but both Newcastle United's goals will have been hauntingly familiar to those who watched Liverpool's title defence collapse under Slot last season.

Newcastle cashed in on Liverpool's wide open midfield, a flaw from the last campaign that saw them so vulnerable to fast counter-attacks. Anthony Elanga sliced through Liverpool for the first then six of Iraola's team stood idly by as Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock combined for the second.

Iraola has suggested Liverpool will not strengthen in midfield with a 'number 6' type defensively-minded player. This early evidence (not to mention what was seen last season) suggests he should.

If not, the draw at Newcastle was a red flag showing Iraola needs to find an internal solution which is not currently obvious.

It's all very well targeting wide players such as Bradley Barcola and Yankuba Minteh, but what about when teams are running straight through the heart of Liverpool's team?

Iraola must also find a way to make the subdued Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz look like the players Liverpool paid £241m for. Both were poor again at St. James' Park.

It looked like it was going to be a losing start for Guardiola's successor before Manchester City pulled it around with two late goals to beat Bournemouth.

How Maresca needed it after City were pounded by Arsenal in the Community Shield. The Italian's emotions at the final whistle looked as much relief as celebration. He needs wins just to settle post-Guardiola nerves and ease the transition.

Maresca described the day as "perfect". It very nearly wasn't.

Erling Haaland's crop is not the only new look at City this season, but on occasions there were passages of play with lots of possession but little punch, a familiar pattern from Maresca's time at Leicester City and Chelsea. The use of Marc Guehi in midfield was a tactical twist.

Maresca will have wanted the win, no matter how it came, and City achieved it, even though it did carry a lot of the hallmarks of a work in progress.

Seconds away from what would have been a very significant win against Liverpool, but still plenty for Jaissle to take away even with the concession of that late, late penalty.

The Toon Army were right behind the new manager and his team, reshaping after the loss of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, and they responded with real intensity.

The effort was there, the attacking style Jaissle wants was there, only the win was missing but enough to please him after fall-out from this summer's Tyneside turbulence.

Poor start for the Austrian who brought FA Cup and Europa League success to Crystal Palace, losing 1-0 to a late Leeds United goal at The City Ground.

Glasner claimed he cannot simply lay hands on players and they perform like "Real Madrid in the 70s", but this still was an unsatisfactory opening as he tries to bring stability and success to Nottingham Forest and their demanding owner Evangelos Marinkis after four managers were in charge last season.

He had no new signings in his starting line-up, with eight from Nuno Espirito Santo's team in the opening-day win over Brentford last season, although it looks like striker Liam Delap might arrive from Chelsea.

Every Forest manager needs wins (and very quickly) so to make a losing introduction was a real blow for Glasner.

title: What does your Premier League club still need in the transfer window?
description: BBC Sport takes a look at what each of the Premier League clubs still need before the summer transfer window shuts in seven days.
fullText:
The first weekend of the Premier League season is complete but clubs still have one week of the transfer window remaining to secure last-minute squad additions.

Results are one thing but for many managers and sporting directors their opening match was an eye-opener in what positions need to be strengthened, who is no longer needed and what gaps still need to be plugged.

With the transfer window closing on Tuesday, 1 September at 23:00 BST, BBC Sport takes a look at what each top-flight club still needs and fans also have their say.

The Premier League champions have already strengthened the middle of the pitch with Bruno Guimaraes, the wing with Christos Tzolis and their defence with Ezri Konsa.

But Arsenal are still in the market for a forward and have a long-standing interest in Julian Alvarez.

Although it appears to be a difficult deal due to many factors, the Gunners will be ready to act if there is a chance to get it done.

If you want someone who is Premier League proven, who has won it all from the World Cup to the Champions League, Julian Alvarez looks like the guy that can take Arsenal to the promised land of finally getting over the line in Europe. Especially when there aren't that many elite forwards in the world.

Alvarez's Arsenal dilemma amid summer's most bitter transfer tussle

Al-Hilal open talks to sign Arsenal winger Martinelli

Nick Mashiter, football reporter

What don't Aston Villa need after a raft of star departures this summer?

Ollie Watkins' transfer saga, with Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal trying to sign the striker, leaves Villa looking for a likely replacement with Nicolas Jackson a target.

A winger is also on the agenda while they need a defender after Ezri Konsa's move to Arsenal, and have opened talks for Club Brugge central defender Joel Ordonez after bids for Southampton centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis were rejected.

It is clear Aston Villa desperately require a striker more than anything right now.

Although I massively rate Victor Lindelof and Pau Torres, the display against Brighton has worried me slightly.

Therefore, I would welcome another centre-back as well.

It looks like we will be OK in midfield once Johan Manzambi is fit and with the addition of Leon Goretzka.

Watkins' departure would cut deepest - and Villa did not see it coming

Villa in talks with Club Brugge for defender Ordonez

Nizaar Kinsella, football reporter

Bournemouth are used to being picked off and will simply be hoping to come through the final eight days of the transfer window unscathed.

It is clear that big clubs are circling for forward Eli Junior Kroupi and midfielder Alex Scott, who the Cherries insist are not for sale.

In terms of incomings, Bournemouth are largely done as they close in on a move for Juventus goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio.

Phil McNulty, chief football writer

Brentford are in the fortunate position of being able to choose their deals carefully after some excellent squad strengthening.

The Bees have been looking at left-back, with West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf strongly linked, but it hardly seems a matter of urgency with Keane Lewis-Potter able to play as a wing-back with Rico Henry and Aaron Hickey also in the mix.

There is experienced striking cover in the shape of former England international Callum Wilson and an all-round depth to Keith Andrews' squad that was missing last season.

Do not expect it to be a hectic closing few days in the transfer window.

Michael Johnston, Brentford fan

Another forward option - particularly down the left - would take this window for Brentford from a nine to a 10 out of 10.

Mykhailo Mudryk's name has been doing the rounds in recent weeks and Brentford have history there, having chased him prior to his move to Chelsea.

Get someone like Mudryk in, and I don't think the transfer window could've gone much better for Andrews.

It is anticipated Yankuba Minteh will leave for Liverpool, which might create space at Brighton for another forward and Carlos Baleba's exit for Manchester United may see the club make a move for midfield reinforcements.

It is possible there may be other exits but, as usual, Brighton will stick to their data driven recruitment plan.

"We must continue to evolve, invest and innovate while remaining true to the principles that have brought us this far," was chairman Tony Bloom's message to fans before the 4-0 win against Aston Villa.

With Baleba's anticipated departure and Minteh looking likely that he might leave as well, we need to bring a defensive midfielder who can bring a physical presence to our midfield and a winger who is proven at the top level.

We have a lot of games this season with European football, so we need to have the squad depth to compete on all fronts if we want to secure a top-10 finish again.

Nizaar Kinsella, football reporter

Chelsea supporters may want another star forward or a new goalkeeper to replace the unconvincing Robert Sanchez, but Xabi Alonso feels his squad is largely complete for this summer.

However, there is a huge amount of work to do to reduce the squad from 39 players to around 25 within the next eight days. That is the priority, as the Blues will not want frustrated players in their squad this season.

Chelsea need to focus more on the outgoings than incoming players.

With no Europe it's important we do not carry a squad that's too heavy, as we won't have too much room for rotation.

If we were to bring anybody in, I think the priority is a top-drawer goalkeeper.

Nick Mashiter, football reporter

Coventry are in the hunt for Mykhailo Mudryk as the Chelsea winger looks to get his career back on track after serving a 20 month suspension for testing positive for banned substance meldonium.

Defensive cover is also likely to be needed by Frank Lampard while players like Luke Woolfenden could leave on loan.

Honestly, I think we have done enough in the transfer window to build a team that can stay up in this league.

There has been a lot of change at Palace with the loss of Maxence Lacroix and a new manager starting the season in Pierre Sage.

The Eagles have been building depth for their Europa League campaign but still need a few bodies in the building.

Sage has made clear he wants a senior centre-back and Palace could be pushed to sign another defender too after the injury to Chadi Riad in the first game of the Premier League season against Everton.

Ollie Thomas, Crystal Palace fan

Riad's injury has amplified the need for another centre-back who is first-team ready.

Axel Disasi is a good start, but a bigger, permanent move would be great. That, plus a central midfielder, and we are set.

Mateta's contract claim leaves Palace with transfer decision

Phil McNulty, chief football writer

Everton simply must sign a recognised right-back before the window shuts. It has been a glaring problem for more than a year.

It is a weakness recognised by everyone at the club but either a prime target cannot be agreed upon or is out of reach.

Talented midfielder Merlin Rohl took on the job for the opening game against Crystal Palace, while Jake O'Brien and James Garner have also been pressed into service.

Time to finally make a decision and get one in. Maybe David Moyes will also look at adding another striker with questions still hanging over Beto and Thierno Barry.

Chelsea outcast Liam Delap is one name regularly linked with Everton.

Nizaar Kinsella, football reporter

Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has been clear that he is happy with the club's business so far, but more could be done to make his squad more balanced.

There have been attempts to sign an additional central defender, with a move for Rennes' Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal explored two weeks ago, and that could be a key area the Cottagers look to strengthen.

This is a club that does not operate at the very top end of the transfer market and one that enjoys a deadline-day deal.

It still feels like Fulham need a right winger - whether that is sticking with Oscar Bobb or providing serious competition for him - I think we need to cover for the loss of Harry Wilson's goals.

We also need a right-sided centre-back as there are serious concerns over how Joachim Anderson will fit Arbeloa's new system.

It has already been a busy summer for Hull City's recruitment team but the ambitious Tigers are still working on adding two new forwards in Mohamed Ali-Cho and Ilyas Ansah.

There has also been interest from the club in Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia, although that deal has taken longer than hoped after the La Liga side raised their valuation of the 20-year-old. Stoke City's Sorba Thomas is also a player of interest.

A goalkeeper, midfielder and right-back also could be on the agenda for Sergej Jakirovic's side in the final week of the window.

Over the next week, if we bring in a left winger, one more striker - assuming the Ali-Cho deal also gets completed - a central midfielder, an attacking midfielder and a right-back to add depth and challenge Lewie Coyle for the starting spot, we will be in a strong position to compete.

Nick Mashiter, football reporter

Ipswich have spent over £150m on 12 new signings since returning to the Premier League.

Boss Gary O'Neil expects more, though, and a striker and a midfielder could arrive at Portman Road.

Fringe players like Anis Memeti could leave as O'Neil shapes his squad.

Having pushed the boat out to sign James Trafford from Manchester City, big money signings are probably off the agenda for Leeds in the last week of the window.

They are interested in taking Mykhailo Mudryk on loan but have not been able to strike a deal with the London club as yet as they are looking at other left wingers.

Leeds are also considering back-up options for forwards Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha and have also been linked with Frankfurt goalkeeper Michael Zetterer, if Lucas Perri joins Torino on loan as expected.

Leeds have had a great transfer window but they badly need another left-footed left-back as cover for Gabriel Gudmundsson.

Beyond that, perhaps another forward or creative midfielder to contend with Harry Wilson, Brenden Aaronson and Noah Okafor.

As has been the case for most of the summer, Liverpool's priority remains the wide attacking areas and the expectation is that at least one and maybe two wingers will come in over the coming week.

Andoni Iraola said that personnel was not the issue when it came to defensive midfielders, the manner in which his side conceded twice at Newcastle would suggest that it would be wise to address Liverpool's deficiencies in that department.

Nahyan Chowdhury, Liverpool fan

It is no secret Liverpool have been actively looking in the market for wingers - Bradley Barcola, Ibrahim Mbaye and Yankuba Minteh - and Sunday's display against Newcastle cemented that with Rio Ngumoha looking uncomfortable on the right.

However, the performance also showed Liverpool may need a defensive midfielder to plug the huge disconnect between the defence and midfield, especially on the counter attack.

Liverpool fans have been crying out for a Fabinho replacement since his departure, but it could be too late with a week to go.

Does Elliott have a Liverpool future after latest omission?

Shamoon Hafez, football reporter

Manchester City could well be one of the busiest sides to do business in the remaining days of the transfer window.

With Savinho gone and Omar Marmoush and Nico Gonzalez seemingly on their way out, there will be gaps in the squad which will need addressing.

A deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi has been agreed with Lille, and with Palmeiras for winger Allan, while BBC Sport has been told winger Pedro Neto remains of interest and speculation around signing Chelsea team-mate Enzo Fernandez continues.

Director of football Hugo Viana may have his hands full in these coming days.

Steven McInerney, Manchester City fan

City need numbers. We have let go of so many players, with Omar Marmoush and maybe Nico Gonzalez set to follow Rodri and Savinho out of the door alongside several others this summer.

It is essential that City bring in three or four new names before the deadline, with two of them being midfielders.

The maths whizz turned £86m teenage star heading to Man City

Man City agree deal for Palmeiras winger Allan

Carlos Baleba's arrival completes the midfield recruitment, now all eyes are on the left-back situation and whether Manchester United bring in someone to compete with Luke Shaw.

The club has a long-standing interest in Newcastle's Lewis Hall, but are also assessing Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and have been heavily linked with Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander.

It is also possible they bring in another forward but that probably depends on one of their existing ones leaving, with Joshua Zirkzee the most likely.

Jay Motty, Manchester United fan

A left-back is essential and this is not just a knee-jerk reaction to the defeat at Hull City - you can see United are short in that position.

We can not realistically expect Luke Shaw to play every game this season and there are still doubts as to whether Michael Carrick trusts Patrick Dorgu in defence.

Baleba completes £70m Man Utd move from Brighton

Man Utd's midfield spending is done - now for a left-back?

Ciaran Kelly, football reporter

Newcastle United's young signings did not look fazed when they faced Liverpool on their Premier League debuts at the weekend.

Manager Matthias Jaissle could still use another midfielder with some top-flight nous, though, after Newcastle sold Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali, and the club are progressing with a move for Manchester City's Nico Gonzalez.

Beyond that, bringing in a mobile and versatile forward who could chip in would help ease the burden on William Osula and Yoane Wissa.

Nick Mashiter, football reporter

Nottingham Forest are still working on deals after only bringing in three new faces so far this summer.

A striker and a full-back would be ideal with the club in talks for Chelsea's Liam Delap, while Fiorentina right-back Dodo is of interest.

Boss Oliver Glasner has played down the need for midfield reinforcements, despite Elliot Anderson's departure to Manchester City.

Forest working on deal for Chelsea striker Delap

With the signings of French full-back Dayann Methalie from Toulouse and Antwerp midfielder Jules Ahoka over the line, the obvious position Sunderland still need to fill is right wing.

Sporting's Geny Catamo is the name most heavily linked.

Asked about reported interest from the Premier League, Sporting boss Rui Borges insisted Catamo is "happy" at the Portuguese club, but we have seen before that does not necessarily mean much.

Given Eliezer Mayenda has left, meaning Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor are the club's only first-team strikers, another forward who plays through the middle is probably needed.

Phil McNulty, chief football writer

Spurs have strengthened by spending heavily in the summer, but if Dominic Solanke is not going to be used regularly as a main striker, then this is where Roberto de Zerbi must look next.

Richarlison took the starting role in the opening weekend loss at Brentford, and while a deal for Manchester City's Omar Marmoush is progressing, is this actually his best role?

Tottenham desperately need forward players who can turn De Zerbi's quick attacks into decisive moments.

Currently Spurs have the players to play through pressure but don't have the players to maximise the situations this creates.

A winger and a striker who can improve us will be a drastic upgrade.

title: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?
description: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
fullText:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

James Trafford (Leeds): It's been a big-pressure move for Trafford going to Leeds. I think at the World Cup with England he thought, 'I should be playing more' and he obviously didn't get the time and needed a move away. He produced a strong performance for Leeds at Nottingham Forest and was one of the few goalkeepers to keep a clean sheet.

Keane Lewis-Potter (Brentford): He was excellent defensively and attacking wise and got his goal. He is one of Brentford's underrated players and sort of sums up their team. Nobody speaks about him or Brentford but they hammered Tottenham.

Nobel Mendy (Hull City): He was so good and powerful. He offered so much defensively to Hull and scored their second goal. He was a real powerhouse. Hull will definitely need him and he is one of those defenders where you think, 'I don't want to play against him'.

Maxence Lacroix (Chelsea): Lacroix just added a level of experience and calmness to Chelsea and also got an assist. He read the game and understood what was needed and provided the maturity that will add so much to Chelsea going forward. It was a very good debut for the France defender.

Maxim de Cuyper (Brighton): He scored two goals and was excellent for Brighton. Opponents Aston Villa were poor, but if you watched the first 20 minutes you would see he was really aggressive and really set the tone with the pressure.

Marc Guehi (Man City): I'll have Guehi in as my holding midfielder. He should have scored two against Bournemouth because he missed a massive chance before he ended up scoring. But he got the equaliser and offered a lot more of a calming presence than City's £116m record signing Elliot Anderson - Guehi controlled the game a little bit more.

Vitaly Janelt (Brentford): He is one of those big, powerful and dominant players who does the basics really well. He mixed that with a goal against Spurs and you don't really speak about him, but he was always the one breaking up play and doing the horrible things really well.

Christos Tzolis (Arsenal): A lot of people are talking about Arsenal and how they're great. That is absolutely true. And so is the bit of business they did bringing this young man in from Club Brugge. So many goals and assists he brings to the team, but also a calming influence and tenacity as well. Look at Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, he feels to me like both of them in one. He has a lot more output than those guys. He's going to be a beast for this year.

Anthony Elanga (Newcastle): Last season I though he was treated poorly by Eddie Howe because he was one that kept being put on the bench, being introduced late or would be the first one to come off. But he showed in a new formation, under a new manager and somebody who believes in him that he can use his pace and power. As a result he looks like a completely different player and he looked happy. He ran past Milos Kerkez like he wasn't there despite the Liverpool left-back having a five-yard start and produced an unbelievable finish for his goal.

Cole Palmer (Chelsea): One we were all talking about, and should've gone to the World Cup with England. Feels like he's got a point to prove, feels like he's been working hard. The injuries from last year skewed everyone's vision. This is going to be a breakout season for him. Everything he did was positive. Ran forward with pace, looked like he could move. He had those issues with the groin but now he's chopping and turning.

Joao Pedro (Chelsea): My old Watford team-mate and someone who will make everyone question when they said he wasn't good enough. He's going to have a breakout year.

Sergej Jakirovic (Hull City): Tactically brilliant and had a gameplan for Manchester United. His side gave a bit of space away but wouldn't get transitioned on, gave away a lot of cheap fouls. Went forward in the wide areas, crossed it and finished the action. He was very impressive in the Championship last year, spoke well but never got too high or too low. He'll take a few by surprise but I'm concerned they won't have the quality in the team. For now, who cares?

title: Does Elliott have a Liverpool future after latest omission?
description: Harvey Elliott's position at Liverpool looks uncertain following his absence from the matchday squad at Newcastle on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.
fullText:
It was a little under a month ago when in the bowels of the Yankee Stadium in New York, Harvey Elliott spoke candidly about his emotions after a "tough" loan spell at Aston Villa and why this summer felt like a second chance for Liverpool.

There was a smile on his face when he spoke about his love for the club - the team he has supported since he was a boy - and wanting to be free and enjoying himself again with his football, because he felt like he had not done that enough.

You only had to see Elliott's joy when he came off the bench in Liverpool's friendly against Monaco earlier this month as all four sides of Anfield stood up and applauded to see what it meant.

With a number of senior first-team players absent, Elliott started Liverpool's first friendly under Andoni Iraola in Nashville and again when Liverpool took on Wrexham in New York four days later but as the World Cup contingent returned, the midfielder was benched and where he stood in the squad became clearer.

On the first weekend of the Premier League season, Elliott was left out of the Liverpool squad entirely for their trip to Newcastle and it now looks increasingly likely that the 23-year-old could be on his way out before the transfer window ends.

Liverpool have received no offers for Elliott - who spent last season on loan at Aston Villa - and his exclusion from the squad on Sunday was not transfer related, nor is the midfielder carrying an injury.

Elliott's contract expires next summer and if first-team football is not possible at Liverpool he needs to go somewhere where it is, to avoid another lost season.

In America, Elliott spoke about how we would speak to Iraola at the "right time" and emphasised the need to be "selfish".

"Ultimately, I'm still wanting to be selfish, doing what's right for me," said Elliott. "Whether that's staying here and fighting for my place or potentially going elsewhere, I'm still unsure at the moment until I get some more intel."

Another year on the fringes would be no good for the man who was named player of the tournament when England Under-21s won the European Championship in 2025.

Elliott played only nine games and a total of 277 minutes after Villa decided early on in the campaign that they did not want to trigger an obligation to sign him from Liverpool for £35m if he made 10 appearances.

Those at Villa stressed Elliott's professionalism and his positivity throughout and to his credit, the attacking midfielder returned early to Liverpool for the start of pre-season after a personally-challenging year.

Iraola himself was impressed by his attitude, saying as much in his introductory press conference.

"I've seen him with this eagerness to show himself. He will have a chance during the pre-season. He came one week earlier and I hope we can see him in a good place," said Iraola.

"Last season had to have been very difficult for him as it was a strange situation that meant they [Aston Villa] couldn't let him play."

In effect, the move to Villa wasted a season of Elliott's career even if he was adamant that it was a "learning curve" in a year where Villa won the Europa League.

"I don't wish it upon any other player, because it's not nice at all," Elliott said.

When he left Liverpool last summer, the primary factor was more game-time after making just one Premier League start during Liverpool's title-winning campaign under Arne Slot in 2024-25.

So with a week to go of the transfer window and with further attacking signings expected at Anfield, perhaps the writing is on the wall.

A move lower down the Premier League or somewhere in Europe may be an option.

After all, this is a player who scored the winner for Liverpool at PSG in a year where the Ligue 1 club won the Champions League.

He is neat on the ball and unafraid to take risks - a return of 15 goals and 21 assists for Liverpool, across all competitions, showcases what he can do.

Either way, it is imperative for all involved that Elliott finds somewhere to play football regularly this season because it seems unlikely at Liverpool and at 23, he cannot afford to have a season like last.

Jean-Philippe Mateta's agents are said to be 'working hard' to find him a new club amid growing uncertainty over his Crystal Palace future.

According to TeamTalk, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur have been contacted to gauge whether they'd be interested in signing the frontman.

His situation at Selhurst Park has turned sour this year, particularly since his proposed £26 million transfer to AC Milan collapsed in the winter window after issues were flagged in his medical regarding a previous meniscus injury.

Although he returned to action for the Eagles and went on to play a key role in their UEFA Conference League triumph, Mateta has still been planning a move elsewhere, despite Palace having no desire to sell him.

He has now raised concerns over their handling of his contract and the validity of the 12-month option triggered by Palace, keeping him tied to the club until June 2027.

Regardless of the outcome of the 29-year-old's dispute, he is keen to seal an agreement with a new club before the September 1 deadline.

United have previously been linked with Mateta, but they have never materialised their interest by submitting a formal bid.

It's thought that INEOS are in the market for a new centre-forward to ease the goalscoring burden on Benjamin Sesko, and while the Palace talisman is slightly older than the players they would usually target, he does now boast six seasons' worth of Premier League experience.

Despite being embroiled in controversy with Palace's board, manager Pierre Sage did opt to start Mateta for the side's season-opener against Everton on Saturday.

He played for just over an hour at the Hill Dickinson Stadium but was unable to make an impact as Palace slumped to a 2-0 defeat.

title: Using international football to reignite Premier League dreams
description: Before his potential Premier League debut for Fulham, BBC Sport looks at the role international football has played in the development of players like Shea Charles.
fullText:
On an August afternoon at Queen Ethelburga's College in York eight years ago, Michael O'Neill could never have known he was about to set eyes upon two players who would go on to become two of his most important Northern Ireland internationals.

It was then that Shea Charles, who has just become NI's most expensive-ever player at the age of 22, and Isaac Price both donned a Northern Ireland shirt for the first time against Leeds United's Under-16s in a friendly.

The duo played as part of a Club NI side - the academy for Northern Ireland at the time - alongside the likes of Liverpool's Conor Bradley and Portsmouth's Terry Devlin.

It was the first step along an international pathway that would see the pair win senior caps as teenagers under O'Neill before they had established themselves at their clubs. Both are now among the first names on the manager's teamsheet.

In the summer window, Charles became the most expensive Northern Ireland footballer when he joined Premier League side Fulham for £30m from Southampton, who he had joined after leaving Manchester City in 2023.

"You could see straight away there was a player there," said O'Neill as he recalled the first time he watched Charles in 2018.

"I suppose that's one of the biggest pleasures we've had with this team because we've known these boys from such a young age."

Charles' rise to NI's most expensive footballer

Dallas backs Charles to thrive at Fulham

As the examples of Charles and his younger brother, Pierce, show, eligibility is key for a nation with a playing pool as small as Northern Ireland.

Sometimes players are scouted, sometimes the parents or agents of players approach the Irish FA, or clubs can alert the association to eligible players.

Sometimes, however, it is a case of being in the right place at the right time.

Joe Shields, who was head of youth recruitment at Manchester City at the time, got to know the Charles family and knew the brothers would be eligible through their mother, Mary, who comes from Northern Ireland.

After watching Shea progress, Shields contacted Andy Cousins, who was also working at City with emerging talent and with the Irish FA, and recommended that it would be good for his development to get involved in the pathway with Northern Ireland.

From there, Cousins introduced O'Neill to the Charles and Price families ahead of their debuts for the Club NI side.

While O'Neill says he was "being polite and saying hello", it also served a bigger purpose. For an up and coming player like Charles, it left a lasting impression.

"It was really cool for us, to be able to see that the senior manager had that interest in the youth team," said midfielder Charles, who has won 35 caps since making his NI debut in March 2023.

"It was really good to see that he does look at those younger age groups and for boys who maybe have a chance to come through.

"It really helped me get to know the boys, the coaches, the whole set-up and eventually going on my first senior camp and making my debut. It was really special and shows that the pathway was really important."

O'Neill says it is important for him to see the next generation of talent long before they get on the fringes of the senior team, and that the work of Andy Waterworth, director of elite player development, and his staff gives him an opportunity to be in the thick of things.

"I think we're really good at that as a small association," he said.

"With the time frame at that age, it can go quite quickly so there's lads I'm seeing in our academy and I may well be the manager that gives that player his debut."

Cousins, who said Charles "didn't have a worry in the world" at City and "just loved playing football", believes that O'Neill's work with the players at a young age allows him to trust them at senior level, which may not happen at other associations.

"It's allowed him to believe in them and put them on the pitch young and early," said Cousins, who now works as head of scouting at Chelsea alongside Shields, who is co-sporting director at Stamford Bridge.

"I think he worries less about the physical elements, and if he thinks they're going to be a really good player long term, it's about getting them in quickly to try and be at that level."

O'Neill says there are two threads to developing Northern Ireland's playing pool, through domestic-based players and those recruited through eligibility.

There are the success stories of Charles and Price, who came through at Everton before establishing himself at senior level with Standard Liege and West Brom.

But O'Neill adds that if a club releases a player or if their future is uncertain, that the JD Academy - the successor to Club NI - offers stability to help them continue to develop as footballers.

O'Neill pointed to the stories of Dan Ballard and Pierce Charles, who were released by Arsenal and Manchester City respectively, but were still selected by Northern Ireland's youth teams to continue their development.

Now, Ballard is a key player for Sunderland - alongside fellow NI defender Trai Hume - and this summer Charles re-joined Manchester City from Sheffield Wednesday before going on loan to Queen's Park Rangers.

"Their futures were very much in the balance. Pierce was released from Man City at 16, but we don't release him from Northern Ireland.

"It's very important to keep the boys involved as much as we can and try and help and support them when those difficult situations arise."

Shea Charles said the story of his brother was "really important" and it was positive for his development to stay involved with Northern Ireland.

"When Pierce left City, he always had those [Northern Ireland underage] games to play in.

"He always had a spot in those teams and was still able to show what he can do at that high level. I feel that can be the same for so many lads."

O'Neill highlighted the example of Ethan Galbraith, who won his first cap as an 18-year-old in 2019 when he was at Manchester United but only broke into the NI team with more regularity when he was 23 and working his way back up the football ladder with Leyton Orient.

With that time and patience, he is now an integral part of O'Neill's squad and earned a move to Stoke City from Swansea in the summer window.

"You can see the potential in all the young players, but their careers never go in an upward straight line all the time," O'Neill added.

"We never write young players off. We understand that at times they may have difficult times at their clubs, but that's natural. It's a competitive environment."

Despite having smaller resource compared to larger nations, O'Neill believes the IFA's scouting team "doesn't miss very much" when it comes to eligibility.

"We're constantly working at it and we're having conversations with various lads who are at different stages of their careers as well.

"I wouldn't ask a young player to do an international transfer unless I thought they genuinely had a chance to come and be a senior international. I think that's very important."

The second strand is with domestic-based players within Northern Ireland.

Of O'Neill's current squad, players like Trai Hume, Conor Bradley, Ethan Galbraith and Ruairi McConville are all graduates from the pathway.

With the next generation, Ceadach O'Neill and Braiden Graham are examples of getting senior Northern Ireland experience while still featuring at underage level for Arsenal and Everton respectively.

Both players have been in the JD Academy and featured for Irish Premiership side Linfield before they made the move to England.

Charles says that while it is a different pathway than the English club system, the benefit of training and playing together has been beneficial for his team-mates.

"The boys talk about how it was really good for them," he said.

"I'm sure it was a bit different to England, but the end goal was always the same to get to the senior squad, so credit to them."

He adds the fact that, no matter where their football journey started, that they have all come through the underage ranks together has been beneficial at senior level.

"I feel like you can see it on the pitch, with the way we play, and how we talk to each other and congratulate each other.

"When we get a bad result, you can see the way we get around each other. It's a really great group."

Before Club NI was formed, there was a community programme but the full JD Academy, as it is now known, allows the most promising young footballers in Northern Ireland to participate in a residential programme at Campbell College, as well as the benefits that come with playing international football at a young age such as nutrition and strength and conditioning.

For O'Neill, it has been one of the "biggest pluses" since he took over as manager for the first time in 2012, saying the academy has done a "phenomenal job".

"I think we have something which a lot of associations are quite jealous of," he said.

"If you're in a big country, the clubs develop the players because they've got the resources to do it, but our clubs can't do that.

"Not every player in the academy is going to go and be a professional player or will play for Northern Ireland at senior international level, but it is giving them a really good opportunity at a critical time in their development path."

While the Championship is a strong league with consistently challenging opposition, playing international football has allowed Charles to play - and hold his own - against some of the best players of the world.

In the past three years, he has faced Rodri for Spain just before they won the European Championships, Germany's Florain Wirtz, Sandro Tonali for Italy and France's midfield pairing of Aurelien Tchouameni and Adrien Rabiot.

On each occasion Charles held his own - particularly against Italy, where he was arguably the best player on the pitch against Tonali and Nicolo Barella.

On Monday night, the 22-year-old could make his Fulham debut against Xabi Alonso's Chelsea, a potential second Premier League appearance coming three years after his debut under Pep Guardiola at City.

It could be a full circle moment for Charles, as he will be reunited with Cousins and Shields, who played a role in the development of the likes of current Chelsea midfielders Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Romeo Lavia, who came through at City alongside Fulham's new recruit.

"It's much easier to benchmark players when you can say that you've played against players from the Premier League or certainly the top five leagues in Europe," said Cousins.

"Especially where the Premier League is so demanding physically, to see people performing well at that level, it's much easier to trust that and to be able to sign a player.

"I think Shea will be absolutely no problem at all, as he's shown in his performances against those big teams he has played against in the last two years."

Charles agrees and says facing the world's best players has helped him prepare for the Premier League.

"To be in that Premier League environment and hopefully to make my Fulham debut on Monday would just be incredible," Charles said.

"It'll be really cool playing the best players in the world every week.

"I look forward to playing with Northern Ireland and being able to experience those games, even if it's a friendly like the Spain or France games.

"It's does prepare you for what the best players are like, so I'm really looking forward to it."
